canonical_topic: Gas Storage Capacity — Base Gas vs Working Gas
definition: A facility's total storage capacity splits into base gas, which is not normally removed, and working gas, which is added and withdrawn during the normal injection and delivery cycle.
core_idea: Only the working-gas portion of a facility's capacity is actively traded; base gas is a cushion that is left in place to support operation.
key_points: Base gas is not normally removed from the facility.
Working gas is the portion added during injection and removed during delivery.
relationships: Explains why aquifers, which have the lowest working-gas-to-total-volume ratio, are the least flexible storage type.
